target.statement: ProReflow-II attains FID = 10.70 on the MS COCO 2014 validation set with only 4 sampling steps (SDv1.5 backbone), close to its 32-step DDIM teacher (FID = 10.05).
target.table_ref: Table 2 (Flow-based methods, ProReflow-II 4 steps); also quoted in the abstract
target.dataset: MS COCO 2014 validation (model trained on 0.8M LAION-Art images)

compute.basis: The metric is produced by a student SDv1.5 UNet trained in three progressive reflow stages (windows 8-4-2, 10000 iterations at batch 256 each), which the paper reports as 6.5 + 8.7 = 15.2 H20-GPU-days on 8 NVIDIA H20 GPUs, plus 32-step DDIM teacher data synthesis and COCO FID/CLIP evaluation - far beyond a CPU laptop (only a GPU-enabled, non-reproducible-in-hours run).

blockers: No code or checkpoint released: the PDF contains no repository link and only states 'Our codes will be released at Github'
Training requires 8 NVIDIA H20 GPUs and ~15.2 H20-GPU-days for the full ProReflow-I + ProReflow-II pipeline (SDXL variant even larger)
Training set is 0.8M LAION-Art images (SDXL variant additionally uses 1.5M laion2B-en-aesthetic samples) - hundreds of GB download, filtering and preprocessing
Teacher-trajectory synthesis needs 32-step DDIM sampling of the frozen SDv1.5 in every training batch, an expensive per-iteration cost that cannot be scaled to few CPU hours
FID evaluation on COCO-2014/2017 at 512x512 with CLIP scoring also needs stable-diffusion-scale inference, impractical on 8 CPU cores
title: ProReflow: Progressive Reflow with Decomposed Velocity
